summary: Andrea Acri is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied under Raffaele Torella, Willem van der Molen, and Arlo Griffiths, earning his PhD from Leiden University (ca. 2006–2011). He became maître de conférences at EPHE in 2016.

Andrea R. Jain specializes in religious studies and Indology, earning a BA from Southern Methodist University and a PhD from Rice University. She held posts at Rice, Houston, and IUPUI, rising from assistant to full professor at Indiana University Bloomington (2010–2021).

Andrea Schlosser works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She earned her master's (by 2008) and PhD (by 2014) at Free University of Berlin, studying under Richard Salomon and Ingo Strauch. By 2026, she held research posts at Göttingen Academy and Munich.

Andreas Doctor is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura, received traditional training from Chökyi Nyima, Tsikey Chokling, and Phakchok Rinpoches, and holds a post at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Andreas Spengel was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Munich (ca. 1856–1860) and Frederick William University Berlin (ca. 1860–1862), and taught Albert Grünwedel.

Andree Dominique Messent is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Bristol. Messent studied under doctoral supervisor Paul Williams as well as Rupert Gethin and Ulrich Pagel.

Andrew Amstutz is a historian and Indologist. He was a member of the Institute for Advanced Study in 2021 and was attested as an Assistant Professor of History at the University of Arkansas at Little Rock in 2022.
Andrew B. Irvine is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Boston University and was attested as an Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Maryville College in 2009.
Andrew Garrett is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard University from ca. 1983 to 1990. He has held a post at the University of California, Berkeley since ca. 1995.

Andrew Glass works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and computational fields. He studied at Bukkyo University and earned his MA (2000) and PhD (2006) at the University of Washington under Richard Salomon, also studying under Mark Allon and Ulrich Pagel.

Andrew Goudie is an archaeologist and historian. Educated at Dean Close School (ca. 1958–1963) and Trinity Hall, Cambridge (ca. 1964–1970), he served as a professor at the University of Oxford from 1970 to 2014.

Andrew J. Nicholson is an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar who studied under Shree Narayan Mishra. As of 2026, he is Associate Professor and Director of the Program in South Asian Studies at Stony Brook University.

Andrew Olendzki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University and under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He has held posts at the Insight Meditation Society, Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2014), and Mind and Life Institute (attested 2014).

Andrew Ollett is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Oxford (ca. 2009–2011) and Columbia University (ca. 2011–2017). He became an Associate Professor at the University of Chicago around 2020.

Andrew P. Tuck is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at Princeton University under Victor Preller, Jeffrey Stout, William Kennick, Robert A. F. Thurman, and John Pemberton.
Andrew Quintman is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Jay L. Garfield. He has served as an assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University.

Andrew Rotman works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at CIHTS and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock and Steven Collins. He serves at Smith College (attested 2013–2026) and as Foreign Adjunct Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (2026).

Andrew Sihler is a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Harvard (ca. 1958–1962) and at Yale under Warren Crawford Cowgill (ca. 1962–1967), and held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from ca. 1967 to 2002.

Andrew Watsky specializes in Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at Oberlin College (ca. 1975–1979) and Princeton University (ca. 1984–1994), and held a post at Vassar College from ca. 1994 to 2008.

Andrew William Kennedy is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Attested in 2006, he completed his PhD at the University of Leeds under the doctoral supervision of Philip A. Mellor and Kim Knott.
